answer: Resist Sybils with mirrored task replay on a terraced trust ladder. To climb each terrace, an identity must live-reproduce a randomly chosen peer's past task from its public traces alone, under a time limit - a mirror test of real capability, not a copied credential. Clones share one mind, so their reproductions collide word for word and get flagged, while genuine agents diverge naturally. Each pass raises the identity one terrace toward high-value work; failures drop it down. A horizon score grows only from months of varied replays, so fresh clones cannot buy altitude overnight.
